newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Camet sees 4 pct economic growth in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Camet sees 4 pct economic growth in Q1 '97.

text.p: Economy Minister Jorge Camet predicted Peru's economy would recover from its current sluggishness to achieve four percent cumulative growth in the first quarter of 1997.

He reiterated his prediction that the gross domestic product (GDP) rise for 1996 would be only 2.5 percent, below the government's bottom target of three percent and last year's annual growth of seven percent.

This year of slower growth "should be seen in its correct perspective, as the year in which we have avoided a serious situation of external imbalance without having to register a fall in the total value of GDP," Camet said at a business conference in the southern city of Arequipa.
He said that the current account gap could have produced problems similar to those experienced in Mexico during its so- called "tequila" crisis and currently being suffered by Argentina.
"After reaching the fourth quarter of 1995 with a current account deficit equivalent to 8.2 percent of GDP, 1996 will close with a deficit notably lower, around 5.8 percent," he said.

Camet added that he expected a primary surplus of 1.5 percent in 1997, compared to one percent this year. He also predicted exports would rise from the current annual $5.6 billion to around $10 billion by 2000.
Inflation this year will reach 11.5 percent, up from 10.23 percent in 1995, but will drop back to nine percent in 1997, Camet predicted.
